title: The Year I Stopped Losing My Friends to a Busy Schedule
script: Narrator: [honestly] For years, I told myself I would call my friends later, when life felt calmer. Later never really came.
Narrator: [thoughtful] My days filled up with work, errands, and small tasks, and my closest friendships slowly grew quiet.
Narrator: [reflective] I never decided to drift away from anyone. It happened slowly, one skipped message at a time.
Narrator: [softly] Then, one evening, a friend from university sent me a message after almost two years of silence.
Narrator: [gently] She said she missed me and wanted to know if I was still the same person she remembered.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Something about that short message made me sit still and think for a long time that night.
Narrator: [honestly] I realized I had almost thirty people saved as friends, but I rarely spoke to any of them anymore.
Narrator: [determined] So I made a small rule for myself. Every week, I would call one friend, just to talk, no real reason needed.
Narrator: [honestly] The first few calls felt awkward, like starting a car that had been sitting still for too long.
Narrator: [warmly] But after a few minutes, old comfort returned, and we laughed like no time had passed between us at all.
Narrator: [reflective] I learned that friendship does not need constant contact, but it does need occasional effort from both sides.
Narrator: [gently] A short message, a quick call, even a simple line like I was thinking of you keeps a bond alive.
Narrator: [warmly] Now I keep a small list of names near my phone, so I remember who I have not called in a while.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Some weeks I miss my own rule completely, and I simply try again the following week instead of giving up.
Narrator: [with a small smile] My friendships feel different now, warmer and more alive, because I finally chose to show up for them.
Narrator: [peacefully] It turns out people rarely forget you completely. They just wait quietly for you to reach out first.
